channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: ICE bought a warehouse in Social Circle, Ga. The city wishes it hadn't
item.description: Communities across the country have been shocked to learn that the Department of Homeland Security wants to use warehouses in their towns for detention space amid the ongoing immigration crackdown. The small Georgia town of Social Circle is one of them.

item.title: Georgia Today: New ICE detention center; HIV prevention medication; Affordable housing
item.description: On the Feb 13th edition: Residents of the city of Social Circle say they're not happy about plans for a new ICE detention facility; Georgia lawmakers pass legislation to boost access to H-I-V prevention medication; And to make housing in Georgia more affordable, some lawmakers say they need to level the playing field.

item.title: GPB evening headlines for February 13, 2026
item.description: The trial of Colin Gray, the father of the accused Apalachee High School shooter, will is set to begin after a jury was seated. Macon-Bibb County officials are laying the foundation for a potential casino on the site of an old mall department store. Georgia Democrats have released plans to increase the supply of affordable housing and crack down on rental abuses.

item.title: DHS says immigration agents appear to have lied about shooting in Minnesota
item.description: Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis was shot in the leg during the incident. Another Venezuelan man was also accused of attacking an immigration officer.

item.title: Lawmakers: Spotlight - Truancy Penalties, Parent Accountability, and Mandatory Kindergarten
item.description: Republican Senator Clint Dixon of Gwinnett County and Democratic Senator Derek Mallow of Savannah discuss chronic absenteeism in Georgia schools and proposed policy solutions. The discussion covers possible penalties for students and parents, updates to truancy reporting, and a proposal to make kindergarten mandatory statewide.

item.title: Kitty cats and cloud hands - how U.S. Olympic snowboarders keep calm in competition
item.description: U.S. snowboarders psych themselves up before competition with heavy metal and pop music, cat photos, and apparently many on the men's halfpipe team now do Qigong.

item.title: It's been five years since catastrophic Texas blackouts. How much has changed?
item.description: Power companies say they're better prepared for extreme weather, but challenges remain to electricity production as the state's demand grows

item.title: Ilia Malinin, U.S. figure skater favored for gold, finishes 8th
item.description: Malinin, undefeated since 2023, stumbled and fell multiple times, landing far off the podium. Mikhail Shaidorov of Kazakhstan won gold in an upset that shocked even himself.

item.title: Venezuela debates sweeping amnesty for political prisoners
item.description: After the fall of Nicolás Maduro, the Venezuelan regime promise amnesty and reconciliation — but for hundreds still jailed and thousands facing charges, justice remains uncertain.

item.title: 5 things to know about the shutdown at the Department of Homeland Security
item.description: The sprawling agency saw its baseline funding expire after lawmakers left town for a week-long recess, but without a deal to rein in the conduct of federal immigration officers.
